newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Straits sees copper decision in mid-98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Straits sees copper decision in mid-98.

text.p: Straits Resources NL said on Thursday it expected to decide by mid-1998 on whether to proceed with its Maroochydore and Tritton copper projects.

Chief executive Brian Rear said Straits would focus in coming months on its Sebuku coal project in Indonesia and getting at least one of the two Australian copper projects to a serious feasibility study.
"They should go to feasibility in mid-this year," Rear told a media briefing after the release of the company's 1996 results. The feasibility studies would take about 12 months.
Rear said Straits, which holds 60 percent of the Girilambone copper mine in New South Wales, aimed to lift its attributable copper production to 30,000 tonnes per year within three years.
Girilambone, owned 40 percent by Nord Pacific Ltd, produced 16,282 tonnes of copper in 1996.
Rear said the Maroochydore project in northern Western Australia would cost up to A$150 million to develop as a mine with a 15-20 year life, planned produce 50,000 tonnes a year of copper cathode.

An updated resource estimate was expected in April or May, while Straits would consider technical aspects such as the amount of acid needed for the production process, which was important due to the site's remote location.
"If all those things confirm work we did last year we would be encouraged enough to push on to a full feasibility study in June or July," he said.
Maroochydore is owned by Murchison United NL, while Straits can earn up to 60 percent of the project through funding evaluation and feasibility work.
Studies last year estimated an inferred resource of 571,000 tonnes of copper.
Rear said the underground Tritton project would cost A$100-A$120 million to develop, and had the potential to produce 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes a year of contained metal in concentrates.
Straits and Nord each hold a 50 percent interest in Tritton, which is located 22 km south of the Girilambone mine.
